title: FeasibilityOpportunitiesComputed
description:
feasibility-service has propagated the constellation over the request's horizon and found at least one geometrically valid acquisition opportunity. An Opportunity is a (satellite, time window, geometry, mode) tuple that a real sensor could fly. It is a CANDIDATE, not a commitment — winning allocation is what turns it into an Acquisition.

This event is the fan-out point of the pipeline: one request produces one of these, carrying up to a few thousand opportunities. That size is why the planner batches by (satellite_id, bucket_start) rather than reacting per-opportunity.

causation_id.description: The event_id of the tasking.request.received.v1 that triggered this sweep.

horizon.description: The interval actually searched. Normally equal to the request window, but clamped to the configured maximum planning horizon — so a customer asking for a 30-day window gets an honest answer about the 7 days we searched, rather than a silent truncation.

tle_references.description: Provenance for every satellite considered, including ones that produced no opportunities. This is what makes a computed window auditable back to the exact element set that produced it — and what makes 'the plan looked wrong because the TLE was two days old' a diagnosable statement rather than a guess.

opportunity_count.description: Length of the opportunities array. Redundant on purpose: consumers log and alert on it without deserialising a multi-megabyte array.

truncated.description: True if more opportunities existed than the configured per-request cap, and the lowest-quality ones were dropped. A silent cap would make the planner look worse than it is for reasons invisible in the data, so the cap is declared.

access_window.description: The interval within which the acquisition may START. The acquisition itself occupies acquisition_duration_s from whatever start the planner chooses. Distinguishing the window from the duration is what gives the planner slack to shift an acquisition and absorb a slew — collapsing them into a fixed interval would throw away the system's main scheduling freedom.

acquisition_duration_s.description: Dwell required for this mode over this target.

orbit_number.description: Revolution number at the time of access. The duty-cycle budget is enforced per orbit, so this is the bucketing key for that knapsack dimension.

footprint.description: Ground footprint the sensor would collect, on the WGS84 ellipsoid. Drives both the containment check against the target and the 2D coverage view.

duty_cycle_cost_s.description: Imaging seconds this acquisition charges against the satellite's per-orbit power and thermal budget. Usually equals acquisition_duration_s, but modes with a warm-up or calibration overhead charge more — which is precisely what makes the duty cycle a knapsack constraint rather than a restatement of the interval constraint.

quality_score.description: Normalised geometric quality, 0..1, derived from where the incidence angle sits in the sensor's band and how far the beam is squinted. A tie-break input to allocation and NOT a value: value comes from the bid and tier. Keeping quality and value separate keeps the mechanism honest.
